_what: Every switch for the automatic bug loop. Change it with `node tools/selfheal/auto.mjs`, not by hand - the frequency also lives in a launchd file, and the command keeps the two in step. Editing this file alone changes the switches but NOT the timer.
_enabled: The master switch. False means the timer can fire and nothing happens - belt and braces, so turning it off does not depend on launchd having been unloaded correctly.
_everyMinutes: How often the loop runs. Triage costs one local Claude Code call per waiting report and nothing when the queue is empty, so a short timer is cheap. Below 2 is refused: the runs would overlap.
_steps: Each stage of the loop, separately switchable. They run in this order and a stage that is off simply does not run; the ones after it still do.

steps._triage: Decide what each new report is. Uses the Claude Code installed on this laptop. Writes a verdict and nothing else.
steps._draftIssues: Turn confirmed real bugs into sanitised draft issues on disk. This CANNOT publish - prepare-issue.mjs has no GitHub call in it at all. Publishing stays a human typing yes into approve-issue.mjs.
steps._notify: Email the people who reported. OFF by default and it should stay off until Sanjay decides otherwise: the moment this is true, the machine writes to real strangers with nobody watching. It also needs RESEND_API_KEY and MAIL_FROM in the job's environment, which are deliberately not on this laptop - so turning this on alone still sends nothing.

_quietHours: Optional. [startHour, endHour] in 24h local time, during which the loop does not run. null means always. Useful once notify is on, so nobody is emailed at 4am.
